1. The appellant in this case was the claimant in a claim petition on file No. 411/Claim instituted on 25.07.2006 before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu on account of physical injuries received by him by the Motor Vehicular Accident caused by offending vehicle No.
JK02AK-8912 which was insured by the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company.

2. The Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu by virtue of an award dated 03.08.2009 came to grant compensation in favour of the appellant/claimant thereby awarding compensation of an amount of Rs. 5,34,000/- in the following manner:
1. For loss of future income Rs. 3,60,000/-
2. For Medical expenses Rs. 14,000/-
3. For pain and sufferings Rs. 80,000/-

sentences.text: 4. For loss of amenities of life Rs. 80,000/-

Total Rs. 5,34,000/-
(Rupees five lac and thirty four thousand only)

3. In the award so passed, the appellant was held entitled to compensation of Rs. 5,34,000/- with simple interest @ 7.5 % per annum came to be allowed on awarded money from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu.

4. The onus to pay the compensation came to be rested upon the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company absolving the owner and driver of the offending vehicle of the liability to this payment of compensation to the petitioner.

5. The respondent No. 1-Insurance Company did not agitate the award of compensation in favour of the petitioner on any ground muchless on the ground of quantum or on the ground of breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

However, the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company came forward with a review petition before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu on file No. 411/Claim seeking review of the award dated 03.08.2009 in the context of proving the fakeness of the driving license of the driver of the offending vehicle and not on any other aspect with respect to the award dated 03.08.2009 in particular the compensation assessed and the interest amount awarded thereupon.

6. Review petition came to be dismissed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu by virtue of an order dated 29.10.2011 with the following observations:
"In the face of aforesaid discussion, there shall be no alteration in the award dated 03.08.2009 passed by this Tribunal and petitioner is held entitled to compensation of Rs. 5,34,000/- along with interest @7.5% from the date of filing of petition till realization of awarded sum, which shall be payable by respondent- Insurance Company as per the terms and conditions mentioned in the award dated 03.08.2009.
Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
File be consigned to records after its due compilation."

7. Upon disposal of the said review petition, the respondent No. 1- Insurance Company came forward to make payment of the compensation amount by way of issuance of two cheques both dated 08.03.2012 for an amount of Rs. 5,07,833/- and Rs. 1,62,698/-.
8.

After having satisfied the said award, it had occurred to the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company that it has made an excess payment of an amount of Rs. 1,39,374/- on account of interest calculated upon the amount of Rs. 3,60,000/- which was one of the components of the award money of Rs.
5,34,000/-.
This component of Rs. 3,60,000/- was on account of loss of future income.

sentences.text: The respondent No. 1-United India Insurance Company reckoned that the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu in its award dated 03.08.2009 had not included the future component of Rs. 3,60,000/- admissible to payment of interest.

10. A careful perusal of the award dated 03.08.2009 would show that the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu did not specify that payment of simple interest of 7.5 % per annum is not to operate with respect to amount of Rs. 3,60,000/-.

11. Although, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu referred to a judgment of this Court in case reported in 2005(2) JKJ 132 (HC) titled "National Insurance Co. Vs. Deep Raj and others" in which it came to be ordered that the award amount to exclude to rate of interest already granted in the whole award, however, on the future earning, the appellant is not to be entitled to any interest by reference to said case.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Vs. Deep Raj and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. Despite the said judgment of this Court, being cited in its award, the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu did not make it a part of its award to say that interest of 7.5% is not to be operated with respect to future loss of income of Rs. 3,60,000/-.

13. For the purpose of seeking recovery, so to say of over payment of amount of Rs. 1,39,374/-, the respondent came forward with an application in the form of a review with respect to order dated 29.10.2011 thereby saying that the over payment of Rs. 1,39,374/- is because of an error obtaining in the order dated 29.10.2011.
14.

This application of the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company came to be allowed on file No.
71-A/Misc. filed on 03.10.2012 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu by virtue of an order dated 28.03.2013 which came to reckon a purported mistake in the order dated 29.10.2011 resulting in payment of the interest on the award amount of Rs. 3,60,000/- and simultaneously dismissed the execution petition of the appellant through which the appellant was seeking recovery of unpaid amount of Rs. 11,000/-, and also calling upon the appellant to deposit the excess payment of interest of Rs. 1,39,374/- with the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT),
Jammu which rendered the appellant/claimant aggrieved to come up with the appeal before this Court.

15. Since, the impugned order dated 28.03.2013 is relatable to the principal award dated 03.08.2009, as such, the present appeal would be read to be referable with the actual award dated 03.08.2009 and, therefore, held to be maintainable.

16. There are two ways of looking at the situation one in the manner as the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu came to have with respect to the impugned order dated viz the passing of order dated 28.03.2013 as if the mistake was on the part of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu in passing of the order dated 29.10.2011.
17.

Another equally plausible view is and to which the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT),
Jammu did not advert to its attention, is that the mistake was actually on the part of the officials of Suresh Singh vs United India Insurance Co. Bahu Plaza on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50948223/
3 the respondent No. 1- Insurance Company in making excess payment of an amount at their own and in order to cover up that default came forward to attribute the excess payment to the interpretation of the order dated 29.10.2011.
18.

sentences.text:
In fact, there is a third situation and which is the correct one and that is the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu in its original award dated 03.08.2009 at no point of time stated exclusion of the amount of Rs. 3,60,000/- on account of loss of future income from bearing interest of 7.5% per annum and, therefore, this aspect ought to have been challenged by the respondent No.
1-Insurance Company in an appeal under section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and not by way of conjuring a plea that it is because of the order dated 29.10.2011 that the over payment of an amount of Rs. 1,39,374/- came to take place which is factually and legally incorrect and hence the impugned order dated 28.03.2013 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu on file No. 71/A/Misc is hereby set aside.

The setting aside of order dated 28.03.2013 of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT), Jammu will not entitle the appellant to seek revival of the execution petition against the respondent No. 1-Insurance Company for the purported recovery of unpaid award money.
19. Disposed of, accordingly.
(RAHUL BHARTI) JUDGE JAMMU 15.05.2024
